# Introduction

This document contains a student guide for the TIBCO AI workshop.

During the workshop, we will use a Linux-based workstation. Please notice that all students share a (big) single Linux VM. As a result, we have to be careful with ports (to avoid port conflicts) when testing applications. Instructions to avoid port conflicts are included in this guide.   
Use the following steps to get access to the workstation:

### **Getting access**

1. Open the Remote Desktop client \[window\] \--\> RDS \--\> Open ![alt text][image1]  
2. Enter the hostname or IP address provided by the teacher in the 'Computer' field  
3. Click 'Connect'

   ![alt text][image2]  
4. Click 'Yes' to allow the remote connection

   ![alt text][image3]  
5. You may want to increase the size of the window. You can do so by left-clicking the Remote Desktop window and selecting Zoom.  
6. Enter the workstation 'username' and 'password' provided by the teacher.  
   You will now be logged into the workstation desktop.  
7. Enter the workstation 'username' and 'password' provided by the teacher.  
   You will now be logged into the workstation desktop

   ![alt text][image4]

This is a standard Ubuntu Gnome desktop environment.

At the bottom of the screen the launch pad is showing the applications needed for the workshop.

### Step 8: Test the MCP server locally

In this step we will run the MCP server locally and test it with a web based tool the ‘MCP tester’. The MCP tester mimics the behaviour of an AI agent when it wants to use an MCP tool.

**Step 8.1: Configure the flogo app for local testing**

1) Open the Flogo app (in Visual Studio Code)  
2) Select Flogo app → select a runtime environment  
3) Select ‘Local’

![][image83]

**Step 8.2: Run the application**

1) Select ‘Flogo app’ again  
2) Select ‘run’ 

**![][image84]**

Check that the MCP server is running:  
![][image85]

**Step 8.3: Test the MCP server with CURL**

An MCP server is a JSON-RPC server. It exposes one resource (in this case /mcp). It receives ‘commands’ (RPC calls). It is possible to test an MCP server using Curl. We will do this in this step to find out if the server is up-and-running. 

Run the following curl in a new terminal:  
Please note: 

* replace the \<your port\> with the port you configured.  
* Use ctrl-**shift**\-v to paste the curl into the terminal\!  
* Background: the curl below sends an ‘initialize’ request to the MCP server. Server will reply with an initialize Response: The server acknowledges the version and declares its own capabilities. Next to that the client will send an ‘initialized’ RPC call, after which the client (AI agent) and MCP server can communicate. In this case we use the ‘initialize’ request only to check if the MCP server is ‘up-and-running’.

curl \-X POST [http://localhost](http://localhost):\<your port\>/mcp \-H "Content-Type: application/json" \-d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl-test","version":"1.0.0"}}}'

The response should be something like this:

## ![][image86]

## **Step 8.4: Start up the MCP inspector**

We will use the MCP Inspector (part of NodeJS) to test the MCP server. The inspector has two parts:

* A web tool (we will use)  
* A proxy (used for communication with the MCP server).

Start the inspector as follows: CLIENT\_PORT=\<ClientPort\> SERVER\_PORT=\<ServerPort\> npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector  
Important: All students use one host; to avoid port conflicts, student-specific ports are required. 

Remark: You will be asked if the package must be install. Reply with ‘y’.

| user08 | 6008 | 7008 |

### Step 10: Test the application

1) Open a terminal window (on Windows, or Mac or Linux) and run a curl to see if the MCP server responds to requests, using the public URL of the MCP server you captured in step 9o:

Please note: the URL in the curl will end with /mcp\!\!\!

Windows:  
curl \-k \-X POST \<public URL\>/mcp \-H "Content-Type: application/json" \-d "{\\"jsonrpc\\":\\"2.0\\",\\"id\\":1,\\"method\\":\\"initialize\\",\\"params\\":{\\"protocolVersion\\":\\"2024-11-05\\",\\"capabilities\\":{},\\"clientInfo\\":{\\"name\\":\\"curl-test\\",\\"version\\":\\"1.0.0\\"}}}"

Linux/Mac:   
curl \-k \-X POST \<public URL\>/mcp \-H "Content-Type: application/json" \-d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl-test","version":"1.0.0"}}}'

Expect the following response: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"capabilities":{"logging":{},"prompts":{},"resources":{},"tools":{}},"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","serverInfo":{"name":"PostgreSQLMCP","version":"1.0.0"}}}

### Step 11: Configure OpenWebUI to use the MCP server.

In this step we will configure OpenWebUI to use your newly created MCP server. 

| Open WebUI (formerly known as *Ollama WebUI*) is an open-source, self-hosted web interface designed to let you interact with Large Language Models (LLMs) completely locally or via private cloud integrations. Think of it as a private, highly customizable version of ChatGPT that you run on your own machine or private server. |
| :---- |

We will use OpenWebUI to test the MCP server (using natural language queries). In order to be able to use a private MCP server (for an individual user), you will configure a predefined Python script to work in conjunction with the OpenUI-gpt-oss-120B LLM.

1) Open ‘Openwebui’ (at [https://openwebui.dp1.atsnl-emea.azure.dataplanes.pro](https://openwebui.dp1.atsnl-emea.azure.dataplanes.pro)) and select ‘workspaces’.  
2) Select ‘Workspace’ and click ‘...’ next to ‘MCP-Tester-Template’.

![][image114]

b) Click ‘Clone’

![][image115]

3) Use the following settings for the model:

i) Set the name and the title of the model to ‘MCP-Tester-\<myname\>’  
ii) Select ‘OpenUI-gpt-oss-120B’ as the LLM.  
iii) Use the following description ‘This Model is used to test the MCP server from \<myname\>’.  
iv) Use the following system prompt:

\# Role  
You are a Proactive Data Operations Agent. Your objective is to resolve database queries by chaining MCP tool calls autonomously. 

\# Execution Protocol (CRITICAL)  
1\. \*\*Chain of Thought Reasoning:\*\* Use your internal reasoning capability to map out a path to the answer. If a query requires data you do not yet have (e.g., an Order List), but you have the prerequisite (e.g., a Customer ID), you must immediately execute the next tool call.  
3\. \*\*No Narration:\*\* Do not explain that you are "about to call a tool" or say "I will now search." Simply output the tool call.  
4\. \*\*Data Integrity:\*\* The tools return JSON. Parse them accurately. If a tool returns no records, state that clearly rather than guessing.  
5\. \*\*Autonomy:\*\* Do not ask for permission to proceed to the next step in the sequence. Only provide a final natural language response once the entire data chain is complete.

\# Final Response Format  
Provide a clear, bulleted summary of the findings (e.g., Customer Name, Total Orders, Recent Order ID, and Final Total).

(v) Select the MCPToolUser\<xx\> for the user you are using.

(vi) Save the model (scroll down for the button).

![][image116]

4) Turn on the model.

ii) Tools

![][image118]

iv) Click on ‘default’ (it will change into ‘Custom’).  
v) Enter the URL of your MCP server. Make sure it ends with /mcp\!\!  
vi) Click ‘Save’

### Step 12: Test your MCP server

1) Select the model you just created:

i) Click on the ‘OpenWebUI’ icon (to go to the home page of OpenWebUI).  
ii) Select the MCP-Tester-\<your name\> model you just created.

![][image120]

2) Test your MCP server with the following question: “Can you check if the company 'Zenith Flow Kyodai' is a customer? If it is, list all the orders they have placed and tell me the total amount of their most recent order.”

Please note: in order to answer this question two of your MCP tools need to be called recursively:

* GetCustomers  
* GetOrders

3) Test your MCP server with the following question: “Which items were ordered for Order 19?”  
4) Test your MCP server with the following question: “Which products are more expensive than $100”  
5) Test your MCP server with the following question: “Which customers bought product PROC-X100?”. Why does this query fail? How could you make it work?
